title: Talking About Things in General
summary: Talk about people, things, activities and subjects in general without the. Use the to identify a particular group, thing or amount that is clear from the context.
learningObjectives: Use plural and uncountable nouns without the when speaking generally.
Use sport, game, language and school-subject names without the in ordinary general statements.
Choose the for specific things or groups identified by an earlier mention or a phrase.
Distinguish general meanings from specific meanings with the same noun.

explanation.heading: General plural and uncountable nouns
explanation.body: When you talk about a whole category rather than particular members, plural countable nouns usually have no article: dogs, books, neighbours. Uncountable nouns also usually have no article when you mean them generally: music, water, coffee, or happiness.
explanation.example: Books can teach us about other places.

explanation.heading: Sports and games
explanation.body: In normal sentences about playing, enjoying or watching a sport or game as an activity, do not add the to its name. Say play tennis, love football and enjoy chess.
explanation.example: My cousin plays volleyball after school.

explanation.heading: Languages and school subjects
explanation.body: Names of languages and subjects usually appear without the when you discuss learning or studying them: Italian, Arabic, biology, history, geography and maths.
explanation.example: Nadia studies chemistry and speaks Spanish.

explanation.heading: The for an identifiable group or thing
explanation.body: Use the if you mean particular people or things that a listener can identify. A phrase such as in this room, from our garden, or that we bought yesterday can identify them. Earlier conversation can identify them too.
explanation.example: I watered the plants on our balcony this morning.

explanation.heading: The same noun can change meaning
explanation.body: A noun can be general in one sentence and specific in another. Coffee is popular means coffee in general. The coffee in my cup means one particular drink. Similarly, history is a school subject, but the history of a town is the story of that particular town.
explanation.example: I like tea, but the tea in this mug is too hot.

comparisons.title: People or things in general versus a particular group

left.label: General
left.note: Birds means birds as a general group, so it takes no article.

right.label: Specific
right.example: The birds outside my window are singing.
right.note: The identifies the birds in this particular place.

comparisons.title: A general substance versus a known amount

left.label: General
left.example: I drink water with every meal.
left.note: Water is an uncountable noun used generally.

right.label: Specific
right.example: The water in this bottle is warm.
right.note: The phrase in this bottle identifies particular water.

examples.note: Plural dogs refers to dogs in general.

examples.sentence: I enjoy listening to classical music.
examples.note: Music is an uncountable noun used generally.

examples.sentence: My friend plays badminton every weekend.
examples.note: Do not use the with a sport name here.
Geography is a subject name and normally has no article.

examples.sentence: I washed the cups we used at breakfast.
examples.note: The cups identifies the particular cups from breakfast.

commonMistakes.incorrect: My favourite kind of music is the jazz.
commonMistakes.correct: My favourite kind of music is jazz.
commonMistakes.why: A music genre used generally, such as jazz, normally has no article.
The sport name badminton is normally used without the.

commonMistakes.incorrect: Leo is studying the history at school.
commonMistakes.correct: Leo is studying history at school.
commonMistakes.why: History as a school subject usually has no article.

commonMistakes.incorrect: I baked some biscuits. Biscuits are on the table.
commonMistakes.correct: I baked some biscuits. The biscuits are on the table.
commonMistakes.why: The biscuits points back to the particular biscuits just mentioned.

studyTips: Before choosing an article, ask whether you mean a general category or a particular group you can identify.
Practise paired examples such as I like coffee and The coffee in this cup is strong.
Remember sport, language and school-subject names as no-article patterns in ordinary sentences.

exercises.prompt: To make a statement about cats in general, complete: ___ often sleep during the day.
exercises.feedback: Cats without an article names the whole category in a general statement.
Tennis is a sport name and normally appears without an article.
Biology is a school or college subject and usually has no article.

exercises.prompt: We have just painted the kitchen. ___ walls are bright yellow now.
exercises.feedback: The walls refers to the particular walls of the kitchen.

exercises.prompt: Complete with “music” and any article needed: I enjoy listening to ___ while I cook.
exercises.feedback: Music refers to music in general here, so no article is needed.

exercises.prompt: Complete with “geography” and any article needed: Daniel studies ___ at school.
exercises.feedback: Geography is a subject name, so we normally use it without the.

exercises.prompt: Complete with the correct article: I bought some apples yesterday. ___ apples are in the kitchen.
exercises.feedback: The apples refers to the particular apples already mentioned.

exercises.prompt: Use the correct article with “history”: I want to learn about ___ history of this town.
exercises.feedback: The history of this town refers to a particular place’s history and needs the.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: I really enjoy the basketball.
exercises.feedback: A sport name normally has no article when you mean the activity.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: She is learning the German at evening classes.
acceptedAnswers: She is learning German at evening classes.
exercises.feedback: Language names such as German normally do not take the.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: I bought three oranges. Oranges are in the fridge.
acceptedAnswers: I bought three oranges. The oranges are in the fridge.
exercises.feedback: The oranges refers to the three oranges already mentioned.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: I met your cousins yesterday. Cousins were very friendly.
acceptedAnswers: I met your cousins yesterday. The cousins were very friendly.
exercises.feedback: The cousins identifies the particular people you just mentioned.

speakingExercises.prompt: Say that you enjoy music. Begin with “I”.
speakingExercises.feedback: Music is used without the when you mean music generally.

speakingExercises.prompt: Say that your friend studies French. Begin with “My friend”.
speakingExercises.feedback: French is a language name, so no article is needed.

speakingExercises.prompt: Say that the flowers in this garden are beautiful. Begin with “The flowers”.
acceptedAnswers: The flowers in this garden are beautiful.
speakingExercises.feedback: The identifies the flowers in a specific garden.

speakingExercises.prompt: State this general fact about the whole animal group: dolphins are mammals. Begin with 'Dolphins', use the present simple, and do not add an article.
speakingExercises.feedback: Plural nouns can describe entire categories without the: dolphins are mammals.

speakingExercises.prompt: Change this sentence from a particular group to bicycles in general. Remove only the unnecessary article and say the whole sentence: 'The bicycles need regular maintenance.'
speakingExercises.feedback: Bicycles without the refers to the general category rather than a known group.

speakingExercises.prompt: A friend asks which school subject Maya studies. The subject is economics. Reply with one sentence beginning 'Maya studies' and do not add an article.
speakingExercises.feedback: A school subject such as economics does not usually take an article.

speakingExercises.prompt: Contrast these facts in one sentence: coffee in general is popular; the coffee in this mug is cold. Begin with 'Coffee is', join the facts with 'but', and use full forms.
acceptedAnswers: Coffee is popular, but the coffee in this mug is cold.
speakingExercises.feedback: Coffee without an article means coffee generally; the coffee in this mug identifies one particular drink.

speakingExercises.prompt: Tell a friend that you enjoy football generally, but dislike the specific match on TV. Begin with 'I enjoy football', join the ideas with 'but', and use 'do not like' rather than a contraction.
acceptedAnswers: I enjoy football, but I do not like the match on TV.
speakingExercises.feedback: Football as a sport has no article; the match on TV identifies a particular match.

listeningExercises.audioText: I really enjoy jazz, but my sister prefers rock music.
listeningExercises.prompt: Which kind of music does the speaker enjoy?
listeningExercises.feedback: The speaker says enjoy jazz, without the, to talk about a type of music generally.

listeningExercises.audioText: We visited a small park, and the trees there were very tall.
listeningExercises.feedback: The trees there points to the trees at the particular park.

listeningExercises.audioText: I like tea, but the tea in this cup is too sweet.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the two-word phrase used for the particular drink, including its article.
listeningExercises.feedback: The tea points to the tea in this specific cup, unlike tea in general.

listeningExercises.audioText: Ben loves dogs, but the dogs in his neighbour's garden keep him awake at night.
listeningExercises.prompt: Which statement best describes Ben's opinion?
choices: He likes dogs generally but is bothered by a particular group.
He prefers his neighbour's dogs to all others.
listeningExercises.feedback: Dogs without the names the group generally; the dogs in a particular garden are the ones causing trouble.

listeningExercises.audioText: Mira studies French after school, and her brother studies the history of their village.
listeningExercises.prompt: What is Mira's brother learning about?
choices: The past of one particular place.
listeningExercises.feedback: The history of their village is a specific place's past, whereas French is a language name.

listeningExercises.audioText: Music helps me concentrate, but the music coming from upstairs is too loud.
listeningExercises.prompt: What contrast does the speaker make?
choices: Music from upstairs is the speaker's favourite.
Music usually helps, but a particular source is distracting.
listeningExercises.feedback: Music is general in the first clause; the music coming from upstairs is specific.

listeningExercises.audioText: Lena studies physics twice a week, and she finds it interesting.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the one-word school subject heard immediately after 'studies'.
listeningExercises.feedback: Physics is the name of a subject and appears without the.

listeningExercises.audioText: The students in our building enjoy volleyball, and they practise after school.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the two-word phrase that identifies the specific group, including its article.
listeningExercises.feedback: The students points to a particular group, while volleyball names a sport without the.
